text: The ATLAS collaboration reported observation of a new boson near 125 GeV in Phys. Lett. B 716 (2012) 1-29, consistent with the Standard Model Higgs. The CMS collaboration independently confirmed the result in the same issue.
A Higgs-like boson with a mass near 125 GeV was observed at the Large Hadron Collider in 2012, consistent with the prediction of the Standard Model of particle physics.
Abbott et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration), Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 061102 (2016), reported GW150914, the first direct detection of gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger.
The first direct detection of gravitational waves came from a binary black hole merger observed in September 2015, confirming a century-old prediction of general relativity.
Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna, and Charpentier demonstrated programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA cleavage by Cas9 in Science 337 (2012) 816-821, enabling modern CRISPR genome editing.
A bacterial Cas9 nuclease can be programmed with a guide RNA to cut specific DNA sequences, and this mechanism forms the basis of modern genome editing.

Claude Shannon's 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication' in the Bell System Technical Journal established channel capacity C = B log2(1 + S/N) for an additive white Gaussian noise channel.
The maximum error-free data rate over a bandwidth-limited channel with additive Gaussian noise is proportional to the bandwidth times the logarithm of one plus the signal-to-noise ratio.
Vaswani et al., 'Attention Is All You Need', NeurIPS 2017 (arXiv:1706.03762), introduced the Transformer architecture that replaced recurrence with scaled dot-product self-attention.
The Transformer architecture replaced recurrent connections with a self-attention mechanism and became the dominant backbone for large language models.

Krizhevsky, Sutskever, and Hinton, 'ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks', NIPS 2012, achieved a top-5 error of 15.3 percent on ILSVRC, far below the 26.2 percent of the runner-up.
A deep convolutional neural network trained on GPUs dramatically improved image classification accuracy on the ImageNet benchmark in 2012, sparking the modern deep learning era.
The 17th CGPM (1983) fixed the speed of light in vacuum at exactly 299,792,458 m/s and redefined the metre accordingly, a definition maintained by the SI brochure published by the BIPM.
The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, and the metre is defined in terms of this constant.
Watson and Crick described the double-helical structure of DNA with antiparallel strands held by base pairing in Nature 171 (1953) 737-738.
Deoxyribonucleic acid is structured as two antiparallel strands wound into a double helix, held together by complementary base pairing.
Edwin Hubble's 1929 paper in PNAS 15, 168-173, reported a linear relation between galactic recession velocity and distance, establishing what is now called Hubble's law.
Distant galaxies recede from the Milky Way at velocities roughly proportional to their distance, indicating that the universe is expanding.
Vine and Matthews, Nature 199 (1963) 947-949, interpreted symmetric magnetic anomalies flanking mid-ocean ridges as evidence for seafloor spreading, a cornerstone of plate tectonics.
Symmetric stripes of alternating magnetic polarity on either side of mid-ocean ridges show that new oceanic crust forms at the ridges and spreads outward.
Novoselov, Geim, and colleagues reported isolation of single-atom-thick graphene by mechanical exfoliation in Science 306 (2004) 666-669, work recognized by the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Graphene, a single-atom-thick sheet of carbon arranged in a hexagonal lattice, was first isolated in 2004 by mechanically exfoliating graphite with adhesive tape.
Bednorz and Muller reported superconductivity above 30 K in Ba-La-Cu-O in Z. Phys. B 64 (1986) 189-193, launching the field of high-temperature cuprate superconductors.
Certain copper-oxide ceramics become superconducting at temperatures well above the liquid helium range, unlike conventional BCS superconductors.
Farman, Gardiner, and Shanklin reported large seasonal losses of total ozone over Halley Bay, Antarctica in Nature 315 (1985) 207-210, the first observation of the ozone hole.
A severe seasonal depletion of stratospheric ozone occurs over Antarctica each southern spring, driven largely by chlorine chemistry from human-made halocarbons.
Alexander Fleming reported the antibacterial action of a Penicillium mold against staphylococci in Br. J. Exp. Pathol. 10 (1929) 226-236, the foundational paper on penicillin.
Penicillin is an antibiotic produced by a Penicillium mold that kills many species of bacteria by disrupting cell wall synthesis.
Polack et al., NEJM 383 (2020) 2603-2615, reported 95 percent efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine against COVID-19 in a randomized placebo-controlled trial of over 43,000 participants.
An mRNA vaccine encoding the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein was shown to be highly effective at preventing symptomatic COVID-19 in large randomized clinical trials.

Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman, 'A Method for Obtaining Digital Signatures and Public-Key Cryptosystems', Commun. ACM 21 (1978) 120-126, introduced the RSA cryptosystem based on the hardness of integer factorization.
The RSA public-key cryptosystem is secure under the assumption that factoring the product of two large primes is computationally intractable.
The Advanced Encryption Standard was specified by NIST in FIPS PUB 197 (2001) based on the Rijndael block cipher designed by Daemen and Rijmen.
The Advanced Encryption Standard is a symmetric block cipher with a 128-bit block and key sizes of 128, 192, or 256 bits, widely used to encrypt data at rest and in transit.
Van Jacobson, 'Congestion Avoidance and Control', SIGCOMM 1988, introduced slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, and fast recovery, now core to TCP.
TCP detects network congestion from packet loss and duplicate acknowledgements and responds by reducing its sending window, then slowly ramping back up.
Leslie Lamport, 'The Part-Time Parliament', ACM TOCS 16 (1998) 133-169, described the Paxos algorithm for reaching consensus in an asynchronous network with crash failures.
Paxos is a fault-tolerant consensus algorithm that lets a set of distributed processes agree on a single value despite crash failures and message loss.
Dean and Ghemawat, 'MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters', OSDI 2004, described Google's programming model for parallel batch processing on commodity clusters.
MapReduce is a programming model for processing large datasets on a cluster by expressing a computation as a map function followed by a shuffle and a reduce function.
Edsger Dijkstra, 'A Note on Two Problems in Connexion with Graphs', Numerische Mathematik 1 (1959) 269-271, presented the single-source shortest path algorithm that bears his name.
Dijkstra's algorithm computes shortest paths from a single source in a graph with non-negative edge weights by repeatedly extracting the nearest unvisited vertex.
The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the existence and smoothness of solutions to the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations as one of the Millennium Prize Problems.
Whether smooth global solutions always exist for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with smooth initial data remains an open problem in mathematics.
Einstein presented the field equations of general relativity in Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. (1915) 844-847, relating spacetime curvature to the stress-energy tensor.
General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of four-dimensional spacetime caused by the distribution of energy and momentum.
Mayor and Queloz, Nature 378 (1995) 355-359, reported the discovery of 51 Pegasi b, the first exoplanet detected orbiting a main-sequence star, by radial velocity measurements.
The first confirmed exoplanet around a Sun-like star was detected in 1995 by measuring periodic Doppler shifts in the host star's spectrum.
Penzias and Wilson, ApJ 142 (1965) 419-421, reported an isotropic 3.5 K excess antenna temperature at 4080 Mc/s, identified by Dicke et al. as the cosmic microwave background.
The cosmic microwave background is a nearly isotropic microwave radiation with a blackbody temperature of about 2.7 Kelvin, a relic of the early hot universe.
Gordon Moore, 'Cramming More Components onto Integrated Circuits', Electronics 38 (1965) 114-117, projected that the number of components per integrated circuit would double roughly every year.
For several decades the number of transistors on a commercial integrated circuit doubled approximately every two years, an empirical trend that shaped the semiconductor industry.
C. A. R. Hoare, 'Quicksort', Computer Journal 5 (1962) 10-16, described the partition-based sorting algorithm with average O(n log n) running time.
Quicksort is a comparison-based sorting algorithm that recursively partitions an array around a pivot and runs in O(n log n) average time.

Alan Turing, 'On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem', Proc. London Math. Soc. s2-42 (1937) 230-265, introduced the Turing machine and proved the undecidability of the halting problem.
There is no general algorithm that can decide, for every program and input, whether the program eventually halts.
Saiki, Mullis et al., Science 230 (1985) 1350-1354, reported the polymerase chain reaction for enzymatic amplification of specific DNA sequences.
The polymerase chain reaction exponentially amplifies a targeted DNA segment through repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing, and enzymatic extension.
Chapin, Fuller, and Pearson, J. Appl. Phys. 25 (1954) 676-677, described the first practical silicon p-n junction solar cell with about 6 percent efficiency.
A silicon p-n junction exposed to sunlight generates an electric current through the photovoltaic effect, forming the basis of modern solar cells.

Goodenough and co-workers reported the LiCoO2 cathode in Mater. Res. Bull. 15 (1980) 783-789, a foundational result for the commercial lithium-ion battery recognized by the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Modern lithium-ion batteries use a layered lithium cobalt oxide cathode paired with a carbon anode and a lithium-salt electrolyte to achieve high energy density.
LIGO Scientific Collaboration, 'Advanced LIGO', Class. Quantum Grav. 32 (2015) 074001, describes the dual-recycled Fabry-Perot Michelson interferometers with 4 km arms.
LIGO detects gravitational waves using kilometre-scale Michelson interferometers with Fabry-Perot cavities in each arm to amplify the signal from passing strains.
The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration, ApJ Lett. 875 (2019) L1, published the first resolved image of the supermassive black hole M87* using very long baseline interferometry at 1.3 mm.
A global network of millimetre-wavelength radio telescopes produced the first resolved image of the shadow of a supermassive black hole at the centre of the galaxy M87.
Gardner et al., Space Science Reviews 123 (2006) 485-606, described the mission concept for the James Webb Space Telescope, a 6.5 m segmented infrared observatory at Sun-Earth L2.
The James Webb Space Telescope is a 6.5 metre segmented infrared observatory parked near the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, designed to observe the early universe.
NASA mission report MR-5, 'Apollo 11 Mission Report' (MSC-00171, 1969), documents the first crewed lunar landing on 20 July 1969 by Armstrong and Aldrin aboard the Eagle lunar module.
The first crewed landing on the Moon occurred on 20 July 1969 when the Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle touched down in the Sea of Tranquility.
The Washington State Report, 'The Failure of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge', Federal Works Agency (1941), documented the 7 November 1940 collapse as an aeroelastic flutter failure.
The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapsed on 7 November 1940 due to aeroelastic flutter, where wind-induced oscillations coupled destructively with the deck's torsional mode.
Rubin and Ford, ApJ 159 (1970) 379-403, measured flat rotation curves of the Andromeda galaxy M31, providing strong evidence for extended dark matter halos.
Rotation curves of spiral galaxies stay roughly flat at large radii instead of falling off, implying the presence of an extended halo of unseen matter.
James Clerk Maxwell, 'A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field', Phil. Trans. R. Soc. 155 (1865) 459-512, unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single field theory.
Electric and magnetic fields are coupled and their dynamics obey a set of four linear partial differential equations, which also predict electromagnetic waves traveling at the speed of light.
Dmitri Mendeleev, Zeitschrift fur Chemie 12 (1869) 405-406, proposed the first widely adopted periodic classification of the elements by atomic weight and recurring chemical properties.
The chemical elements can be arranged in a table where columns group elements with similar chemical properties and rows correspond to filling of electron shells.
Fritz Haber's 1918 Nobel lecture described the synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen over an iron catalyst at high pressure, industrialized by Carl Bosch at BASF.
Ammonia is produced industrially by combining nitrogen and hydrogen gas at high temperature and pressure over an iron-based catalyst, enabling modern fertilizer production.
Black and Scholes, J. Political Economy 81 (1973) 637-654, derived the closed-form price of a European option under geometric Brownian motion and no arbitrage.
Under assumptions of geometric Brownian motion for the underlying asset and no arbitrage, the price of a European option is given by a closed-form formula.
Rekhter, Li, and Hares, RFC 4271, 'A Border Gateway Protocol 4 (BGP-4)', IETF (2006), specifies the path-vector routing protocol used between autonomous systems on the Internet.
The Border Gateway Protocol is the path-vector routing protocol that exchanges reachability information between autonomous systems and determines the topology of the global Internet.
Eric Rescorla, RFC 8446, 'The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3', IETF (2018), specifies the cipher-suite negotiation, handshake, and key schedule for TLS 1.3.
TLS 1.3 reduces the handshake to one round trip, drops legacy cipher suites, and always provides forward secrecy through ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
IEEE Std 754-2008 specifies the binary and decimal floating-point formats, rounding rules, and exceptional value handling used on essentially all modern CPUs and GPUs.
The widely used binary32 and binary64 floating-point formats define a 1-bit sign, an exponent field, and a fraction field, together with rules for rounding and for infinities and NaNs.
Harry Nyquist, Trans. AIEE 47 (1928) 617-644, showed that a band-limited signal of bandwidth B can be reconstructed from samples taken at a rate of at least 2B per second.
A continuous signal that contains no frequencies above B hertz can be perfectly reconstructed from samples taken at a rate of at least twice B per second.
Jumper et al., 'Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold', Nature 596 (2021) 583-589, reported near-experimental accuracy on the CASP14 targets.
Deep learning models can now predict the three-dimensional structure of most proteins from their amino-acid sequence with accuracy approaching experimental methods.

International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium, Nature 409 (2001) 860-921, reported the initial sequence and analysis of the human genome, with Venter et al., Science 291 (2001) 1304-1351, publishing a concurrent private-sector assembly.
The human genome comprises roughly three billion base pairs arranged into twenty-three chromosome pairs, with the first working draft published in 2001.
Glashow, Weinberg, and Salam developed the electroweak unification for which they shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics, combined with QCD to form the Standard Model.
The Standard Model of particle physics unifies the electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions as gauge theories and describes all known elementary particles except gravitons.
NASA/JPL mission report, 'Mars Science Laboratory Entry, Descent, and Landing', JPL D-75929 (2014), describes the sky-crane landing of the Curiosity rover in Gale Crater on 6 August 2012.
NASA's Curiosity rover landed in Gale Crater on Mars on 6 August 2012 using a sky-crane system in which a hovering descent stage lowered the rover to the surface on cables.

IPCC AR6 Working Group I report (2021), Chapter 7, assesses the equilibrium climate sensitivity to a doubling of atmospheric CO2 as very likely in the range 2.0 to 5.0 degrees Celsius with a best estimate of 3.0.
The equilibrium warming from doubling the atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration is very likely between 2 and 5 degrees Celsius, with a best estimate around 3 degrees.
RFC 9110 section 9.3.1 defines GET as a method whose semantics are safe and idempotent, meaning the request is not intended to cause state change on the origin server.
HTTP GET requests are supposed to be safe and idempotent; they shouldn't mutate server state.
RFC 7519 specifies that a JWT is a compact, URL-safe token consisting of three base64url-encoded segments separated by dots: header, payload, and signature.
A JSON Web Token is made up of three base64url parts joined by dots: a header, a payload, and a signature.
Per RFC 6749, the authorization code grant flow requires the client to exchange an authorization code for an access token at the token endpoint using client credentials.
In the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, the client swaps the code for an access token at the token endpoint using its credentials.
RFC 5321 states that an SMTP server MUST accept messages with line lengths of up to 998 octets plus the trailing CRLF.
SMTP servers must handle message lines up to 998 bytes long, not counting the terminating CRLF.
RFC 8259 mandates that JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8.
Interoperable JSON on the wire has to be UTF-8 encoded.
Per the PostgreSQL 16 documentation on Write-Ahead Logging, WAL records are flushed to disk before the corresponding data pages, ensuring crash recovery can replay committed changes.
Postgres flushes WAL records to disk ahead of the actual data pages so crash recovery can redo committed transactions.
The PostgreSQL documentation on concurrency control explains that MVCC gives each transaction a snapshot of the database so readers never block writers and vice versa.
Postgres uses MVCC so readers and writers don't block each other — each transaction sees its own snapshot.
Per the PostgreSQL docs on routine maintenance, autovacuum must run regularly to reclaim space from dead tuples and prevent transaction ID wraparound.
Autovacuum in Postgres has to run often enough to clean up dead tuples and avoid transaction ID wraparound.
The Kubernetes API reference v1.29 states that a Pod's restartPolicy field only applies to containers in the same Pod and defaults to Always.
A Pod's restartPolicy governs only the containers inside that Pod and defaults to Always.
Per the Kubernetes documentation on Services, a ClusterIP service exposes the service on an internal IP reachable only from within the cluster.
Kubernetes ClusterIP services are only reachable from inside the cluster via an internal IP.
The Docker documentation on BuildKit explains that each instruction in a Dockerfile creates a cacheable layer keyed by its inputs, and cache is invalidated when an instruction's inputs change.
Docker build layers are cached per instruction, and changing an instruction's inputs busts the cache for that layer onward.
Per the Docker Compose specification v2, the 'depends_on' key only controls start order and does not wait for the referenced service to be ready unless a healthcheck condition is specified.
In Compose, depends_on only orders startup; it doesn't wait for readiness unless you add a healthcheck condition.
The CPython documentation on threading notes that the Global Interpreter Lock allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time, even on multi-core systems.
CPython's GIL means only one thread runs Python bytecode at a time, regardless of how many cores you have.
PEP 8 recommends limiting all lines to a maximum of 79 characters and docstrings or comments to 72 characters.
Python code should keep lines at or below 79 characters and comments below 72.
PEP 484 introduces a standard syntax for type hints using annotations, which the runtime ignores but static checkers like mypy consume.
Python type hints are evaluated by static checkers like mypy and ignored at runtime.
The Go language specification defines a goroutine as a lightweight thread managed by the Go runtime, started with the 'go' keyword preceding a function call.
Goroutines are Go-runtime-managed lightweight threads launched by prefixing a call with 'go'.
Per the Rust reference on ownership, each value has exactly one owner and is dropped when the owner goes out of scope.
In Rust, every value has one owner, and when that owner goes out of scope the value is dropped.
RFC 9293 describes the TCP three-way handshake: SYN from client, SYN-ACK from server, ACK from client, establishing a full-duplex connection.
TCP opens a connection with a three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, then ACK.
RFC 8446 specifies TLS 1.3, which reduces the handshake to one round trip and removes support for legacy ciphers like RC4 and 3DES.
TLS 1.3 has a single round-trip handshake and drops legacy ciphers such as RC4 and 3DES.
RFC 1035 specifies that DNS messages over UDP are limited to 512 octets unless EDNS0 signals a larger buffer.
DNS over UDP caps at 512 bytes per message unless EDNS0 negotiates a bigger size.
The POSIX.1-2017 standard specifies that fork() returns zero in the child process and the child's PID in the parent process.
After fork(), the child receives a return value of 0 and the parent receives the child's PID.
Per POSIX, SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored by the receiving process.
Processes cannot handle or mask SIGKILL or SIGSTOP.
The W3C CSS Flexbox Level 1 specification defines justify-content as controlling the alignment of flex items along the main axis of the flex container.
In CSS flexbox, justify-content aligns items along the main axis.
The WHATWG HTML Living Standard specifies that a script tag with 'defer' is executed after the document has been parsed but before DOMContentLoaded.
Defer scripts run after HTML parsing finishes but before DOMContentLoaded fires.
The ECMAScript 2024 specification defines strict equality (===) as returning true only when the operands share the same type and value, without type coercion.
JavaScript's === returns true only when both sides match in type and value with no coercion.
Per the React 18 documentation on useEffect, the effect is re-run whenever a value in the dependency array changes by Object.is comparison.
React's useEffect re-runs when any value in its dependency array changes via Object.is.
The PyTorch documentation on autograd states that gradients accumulate in .grad attributes until explicitly zeroed with optimizer.zero_grad() or tensor.grad.zero_().
PyTorch accumulates gradients in .grad until you zero them out; otherwise successive backward calls compound.
The Hugging Face Transformers documentation on tokenizers notes that AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained downloads the tokenizer config, vocab, and merges from the model repo on the Hub.
AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained pulls the tokenizer config, vocabulary, and merges from the Hub.
Per the TensorFlow 2 documentation, tf.function traces Python code into a callable graph, giving graph-mode performance while preserving an eager-mode authoring experience.
TF 2's tf.function turns Python into a traced graph so you get graph-mode speed but write code eagerly.
The OpenAI API reference for chat completions specifies that the 'temperature' parameter ranges from 0 to 2, with higher values producing more random outputs.
OpenAI's chat completion temperature goes from 0 to 2; higher means more random sampling.
Per the Anthropic API documentation, the 'stop_sequences' parameter accepts up to four strings that will cause the model to halt generation when produced.
Anthropic's Messages API accepts up to four stop sequences; generation halts when the model emits one.
The Redis documentation on persistence explains that RDB snapshots are point-in-time dumps while AOF logs every write command, and both can be enabled together.
Redis can persist with RDB point-in-time snapshots, AOF command logs, or both at once.
Per the MongoDB 7 documentation on indexes, a compound index supports queries that filter on a prefix of the indexed fields in the order they were declared.
MongoDB compound indexes help any query that uses a left-to-right prefix of the declared fields.
The Git documentation on git-rebase warns that rebasing commits already pushed to a shared branch rewrites history and forces collaborators to reset their local copies.
Rebasing already-pushed commits on a shared branch rewrites history and breaks other people's local branches.
The Linux kernel documentation on cgroups v2 states that a process can only belong to one cgroup in each hierarchy at a time.
Under cgroups v2, a process is in exactly one cgroup per hierarchy.
The Nginx documentation recommends setting worker_processes to 'auto' so the server spawns one worker per available CPU core.
Nginx's worker_processes 'auto' setting creates one worker per CPU core.
The GraphQL June 2018 specification defines three operation types: query, mutation, and subscription, with query as the default when the operation keyword is omitted.
GraphQL has queries, mutations, and subscriptions, and unmarked operations are treated as queries.
Per the gRPC documentation, the four supported RPC styles are unary, server streaming, client streaming, and bidirectional streaming.
gRPC offers unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional-streaming RPCs.
The Protocol Buffers language guide for proto3 states that scalar fields have default values and are not serialized when set to their default.
In proto3, scalar fields at their default values are skipped on the wire.
Per the AWS S3 documentation, objects uploaded via multipart upload must have each part at least 5 MB except for the final part.
S3 multipart upload parts must be 5 MB or larger, except the last one.
The AWS IAM documentation on policy evaluation states that an explicit Deny in any applicable policy overrides any Allow.
If any IAM policy explicitly denies an action, the request is denied regardless of other allows.
Per the Terraform documentation, the state file maps real-world resources to the configuration and must be shared via a remote backend when working in a team.
Terraform's state maps resources to config and should live in a remote backend for team workflows.
The Ansible documentation on module design emphasizes that modules should be idempotent, producing the same end state whether run once or many times.
Ansible modules are expected to be idempotent — running them repeatedly yields the same end state.
Per the NumPy documentation on broadcasting, two array shapes are compatible when, aligned from the trailing axis, each dimension is either equal or one of them is 1.
NumPy broadcasts two arrays when, aligned from the right, each dimension matches or one equals 1.
The Pandas 2.2 documentation warns that the 'inplace' parameter is being deprecated because it does not reliably avoid copies and complicates method chaining.
Pandas is phasing out the inplace parameter since it doesn't really avoid copies and hurts chaining.
Per the scikit-learn documentation, StandardScaler removes the mean and scales to unit variance using statistics fit on the training data only.
StandardScaler centers and scales features using stats fit from the training set.
The NVIDIA CUDA C++ Programming Guide specifies that threads within a warp execute the same instruction at the same time, and divergent branches are serialized.
CUDA warp threads run in lockstep; branches that diverge within a warp run serially.
The Unicode Standard version 15 specifies that code points in the range U+D800 to U+DFFF are surrogate code points reserved for UTF-16 and are not valid in UTF-8.
Surrogate code points U+D800 through U+DFFF belong to UTF-16 and must not appear in UTF-8.
The Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification states that a MAJOR version increment signals incompatible API changes, while MINOR adds functionality in a backward-compatible way.
SemVer bumps MAJOR for breaking API changes and MINOR for backward-compatible features.
The WebAssembly Core Specification 2.0 defines a linear memory as a contiguous, byte-addressable array that can be grown in pages of 64 KiB.
WebAssembly linear memory is a contiguous byte array that grows in 64 KiB pages.
Marbury v. Madison (1803) established the principle that the Supreme Court has the power to strike down acts of Congress that conflict with the Constitution.
The Supreme Court has the power to invalidate federal laws that it finds to be unconstitutional.
Brown v. Board of Education (1954) held that racial segregation of children in public schools is unconstitutional.
Racial segregation of students in public schools violates the constitutional guarantee of equal protection.
Miranda v. Arizona (1966) requires police to inform suspects in custody of their right to remain silent and their right to an attorney before interrogation.
Before questioning a person held in custody, the police must notify them of their right to stay silent and to have a lawyer present.
Article 17 of the General Data Protection Regulation grants data subjects the right to obtain the erasure of their personal data without undue delay.
Individuals in the European Union may require a controller to delete their personal data without undue delay.
Article 6 of the General Data Protection Regulation enumerates the six lawful bases on which personal data may be processed.
Processing personal data in the European Union is only lawful if it rests on one of six enumerated legal grounds.
Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act shields interactive computer service providers from being treated as the publisher of content posted by their users.
Online platforms in the United States are generally not liable as publishers for content that third-party users post on them.
17 U.S.C. section 302 fixes the term of copyright for works created on or after January 1, 1978 at the life of the author plus seventy years.
Copyright in the United States for works created after 1977 lasts for the life of the author plus seventy years.
17 U.S.C. section 107 codifies the fair use defense to copyright infringement and lists the four factors courts weigh.
Using a copyrighted work without permission may be permitted in the United States if the use qualifies as fair use under a four-factor balancing test.
35 U.S.C. section 102 bars the patenting of inventions that were already publicly known, used, patented, or described in a printed publication before the effective filing date.
An invention cannot receive a United States patent if it was publicly disclosed before the application's effective filing date.
The Lanham Act, codified at 15 U.S.C. sections 1051 and following, governs federal trademark registration and infringement in the United States.
Federal trademark registration and infringement claims in the United States are governed by a single statutory scheme.
Section 2-201 of the Uniform Commercial Code requires contracts for the sale of goods for $500 or more to be in writing to be enforceable.
A contract to sell goods worth five hundred dollars or more must generally be evidenced by a writing to be enforceable in most United States jurisdictions.
Section 2-601 of the Uniform Commercial Code allows a buyer to reject goods that fail in any respect to conform to the contract.
A buyer of goods may reject the entire shipment if it deviates in any respect from what the contract required.
The Restatement (Second) of Contracts section 71 defines consideration as a performance or return promise that is bargained for.
A promise is enforceable as a contract only if each party bargains for and gives something of legal value in exchange.
Palsgraf v. Long Island Railroad Co. (1928) limited a defendant's negligence liability to plaintiffs within the foreseeable zone of danger.
A defendant's duty of care in negligence extends only to plaintiffs whose injury was a foreseeable consequence of the defendant's conduct.
Section 402A of the Restatement (Second) of Torts imposes strict liability on sellers of products that are in a defective condition unreasonably dangerous to the user.
A seller is strictly liable for harm caused by a product sold in a defective condition that is unreasonably dangerous to the consumer.
M'Naghten's Case (1843) set out the common law test that a defendant is not criminally responsible if, due to mental disease, they did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong.
Under the traditional common law insanity test, a defendant is not criminally responsible when a mental disease prevents them from knowing the nature or wrongfulness of the act.
Mapp v. Ohio (1961) applied the Fourth Amendment exclusionary rule to state criminal prosecutions through the Fourteenth Amendment.
Evidence obtained in violation of constitutional search and seizure protections is inadmissible in state criminal trials.
Gideon v. Wainwright (1963) held that the Sixth Amendment guarantees indigent criminal defendants the right to appointed counsel in state felony cases.
An indigent person charged with a state felony has a constitutional right to have an attorney appointed at public expense.
Article 33 of the 1951 Refugee Convention prohibits the expulsion or return of a refugee to a territory where their life or freedom would be threatened.
A state party to the main international refugee treaty may not send a refugee back to a country where their life or freedom would be at risk.
Common Article 3 of the 1949 Geneva Conventions prohibits violence, torture, and outrages upon personal dignity against persons not taking active part in hostilities.
International humanitarian law forbids torture and degrading treatment of civilians and other persons who are not actively participating in an armed conflict.
Article 26 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties codifies the pacta sunt servanda rule that every treaty in force binds its parties and must be performed in good faith.
Every treaty in force obliges its parties to perform their obligations in good faith.
Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter prohibits member states from using force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any state.
Member states of the United Nations are forbidden from using armed force against another state's territorial integrity or political independence.
The National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 requires federal agencies to prepare an environmental impact statement for major federal actions significantly affecting the environment.
United States federal agencies must produce a detailed environmental impact statement before taking major actions that significantly affect the environment.
Section 109 of the Clean Air Act directs the Environmental Protection Agency to set National Ambient Air Quality Standards for criteria pollutants.
The federal environmental regulator must establish nationwide ambient air quality standards for designated pollutants.
Article 2 of the Paris Agreement commits parties to holding the increase in global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
Parties to the landmark international climate accord have agreed to keep global average warming well below two degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
Chevron U.S.A., Inc. v. Natural Resources Defense Council (1984) required courts to defer to a federal agency's reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous statute it administers.
Courts historically deferred to reasonable agency interpretations when the statute an agency administers is ambiguous.
Section 553 of the Administrative Procedure Act requires federal agencies to provide notice of proposed rulemaking and an opportunity for public comment.
Federal agencies in the United States must generally publish a notice of proposed rulemaking and accept public comments before issuing binding regulations.
Section 61 of the Internal Revenue Code defines gross income as all income from whatever source derived.
For United States federal income tax purposes, gross income broadly includes income from any source unless a specific exception applies.
Section 170 of the Internal Revenue Code permits individual taxpayers to deduct qualifying contributions to charitable organizations, subject to percentage limits.
United States individual taxpayers may deduct charitable contributions to qualifying organizations up to statutory percentage limits.
Section 1221 of the Internal Revenue Code defines a capital asset for purposes of computing capital gains and losses.
United States tax law provides a statutory definition of a capital asset used when computing capital gains and losses.
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits employers with fifteen or more employees from discriminating on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
Employers in the United States above a size threshold may not discriminate in employment based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 requires covered employers to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified employees with disabilities unless doing so causes undue hardship.
United States employers must provide reasonable workplace accommodations to qualified disabled employees unless the accommodation would impose undue hardship.
Section 207 of the Fair Labor Standards Act requires employers to pay non-exempt employees overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours worked beyond forty in a workweek.
Non-exempt United States workers must be paid overtime at time and a half for hours worked beyond forty in a single workweek.
Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act protects the right of employees to engage in concerted activities for mutual aid or protection.
Private-sector workers in the United States have a protected legal right to act together for mutual aid or protection.
Rule 10b-5 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 prohibits fraud, misrepresentation, and deceit in connection with the purchase or sale of any security.
United States securities law prohibits fraudulent or deceptive conduct in connection with any securities transaction.
Section 5 of the Securities Act of 1933 generally prohibits the offer or sale of securities unless a registration statement is in effect, absent an exemption.
Issuers may not offer or sell securities to the United States public unless the offering is registered or qualifies for an exemption.
Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 makes illegal every contract, combination, or conspiracy in restraint of trade or commerce.
Any agreement that unreasonably restrains trade or commerce is illegal under United States antitrust law.
Section 362 of the Bankruptcy Code imposes an automatic stay on most collection actions against a debtor upon the filing of a bankruptcy petition.
Filing a bankruptcy petition in the United States automatically halts most collection actions against the debtor.
Section 727 of the Bankruptcy Code grants an individual debtor a discharge of most prepetition debts in a Chapter 7 liquidation case.
An individual who completes a liquidation bankruptcy in the United States generally receives a discharge of most prepetition debts.

The doctrine of adverse possession, as set out in the Restatement (First) of Property section 222, allows a possessor of land to acquire title through open, notorious, continuous, and hostile possession for the statutory period.
A person who openly, notoriously, continuously, and hostilely possesses land for the statutory period can acquire legal title to it.
Section 208 of the Immigration and Nationality Act authorizes the grant of asylum to an applicant who qualifies as a refugee.
A person in the United States who meets the legal definition of a refugee may be granted asylum by the government.
28 U.S.C. section 1332 grants federal district courts diversity jurisdiction over civil actions between citizens of different states where the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.
United States federal district courts may hear civil suits between citizens of different states when more than seventy-five thousand dollars is at stake.
Rule 12(b)(6) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure permits a defendant to move to dismiss a complaint for failure to state a claim upon which relief can be granted.
A defendant in a United States federal civil case can seek early dismissal of a complaint that does not state a legally sufficient claim.
Rule 802 of the Federal Rules of Evidence generally renders hearsay inadmissible unless an exception applies.
Out-of-court statements offered for the truth of the matter asserted are generally inadmissible in federal court unless an exception applies.
Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) held that the Fourteenth Amendment requires all states to license and recognize marriages between two people of the same sex.
States in the United States must issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples and recognize such marriages validly performed elsewhere.
The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 Privacy Rule, codified at 45 C.F.R. Part 164, restricts the uses and disclosures of protected health information by covered entities.
Covered healthcare providers and insurers in the United States face regulatory limits on how they may use and disclose a patient's health information.

The California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, codified at California Civil Code section 1798.100 and following, grants California residents the right to know what personal information businesses collect about them.
Residents of California have a legal right to request from businesses the categories and specific pieces of personal information collected about them.
Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights protects the right to respect for private and family life, home, and correspondence.
States parties to the main European human rights treaty must respect individuals' private and family life, home, and correspondence.
Article I of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade sets out the most-favored-nation obligation that any advantage granted to one contracting party must be extended to all others.
Under the foundational multilateral trade treaty, any trade advantage one state grants must be extended unconditionally to all other state parties.

Article 3 of the United Nations Convention against Torture prohibits state parties from expelling, returning, or extraditing a person to a state where there are substantial grounds for believing they would be subjected to torture.
A state may not deport or extradite a person to a country where they would face a substantial risk of being tortured.

The SPRINT trial published in NEJM in 2015 found that targeting systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg cut major cardiovascular events by about 25 percent versus the standard target of 140 mmHg in high-risk non-diabetic adults.
Driving systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg in high-risk non-diabetic adults reduces major cardiovascular events by roughly a quarter compared with the usual 140 mmHg target.

The Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' Collaboration meta-analysis in The Lancet showed that each 1 mmol/L reduction in LDL cholesterol on statin therapy produces roughly a 22 percent drop in major vascular events per year of treatment.
Every 1 mmol/L that statins pull LDL cholesterol down translates into about a 22 percent lower annual rate of major vascular events.

The ASPREE trial reported in NEJM in 2018 that daily low-dose aspirin in healthy older adults did not reduce cardiovascular events but did raise major bleeding, arguing against routine primary prevention aspirin over age 70.

For healthy adults over 70, taking low-dose aspirin every day does not lower heart attack or stroke risk and noticeably increases major bleeding, so it is no longer recommended for primary prevention.
The USPSTF 2024 recommendation statement now advises biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 at average risk, a shift from the prior age 50 start.
Average-risk women should start getting a screening mammogram every two years from age 40, not from 50 as previously advised.
The USPSTF 2021 guideline lowered the recommended starting age for colorectal cancer screening from 50 to 45 for average-risk adults, citing rising early-onset incidence.
Routine colorectal cancer screening should now begin at age 45 rather than 50 for adults at average risk.

A Cochrane systematic review of HPV vaccine randomized trials concluded that vaccinating adolescent girls before sexual debut substantially reduces the incidence of high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia.
Vaccinating adolescent girls against HPV before they become sexually active sharply cuts the rate of high-grade cervical precancerous lesions.

The National Lung Screening Trial, reported in NEJM in 2011, showed that low-dose CT screening reduced lung cancer mortality by 20 percent compared with chest X-ray in heavy-smoking adults aged 55 to 74.
Heavy smokers aged 55 to 74 who get annual low-dose CT scans are about 20 percent less likely to die from lung cancer than those screened only with chest X-ray.

The WHO position paper on measles vaccines states that two doses of measles-containing vaccine confer roughly 97 percent protection against measles and are required for herd immunity thresholds around 95 percent coverage.
Two doses of a measles vaccine give about 97 percent individual protection, and reaching herd immunity against measles needs roughly 95 percent community coverage.

The iPrEx trial published in NEJM in 2010 demonstrated that daily oral tenofovir-emtricitabine reduced HIV acquisition by 44 percent overall and by more than 90 percent among participants with detectable drug levels.
Taking daily oral tenofovir-emtricitabine as PrEP cuts HIV acquisition by about 44 percent on average and by over 90 percent in people who actually take it consistently.

Polack and colleagues reported in NEJM in 2020 that two doses of the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine conferred 95 percent efficacy against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection in the pivotal phase 3 trial.
Two doses of the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine were 95 percent effective at preventing symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection in the pivotal phase 3 trial.
The WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care report that adherence to the five moments of hand hygiene reduces healthcare-associated infection rates by 30 to 40 percent in acute-care settings.
Following the five moments of hand hygiene in acute-care wards drops healthcare-associated infection rates by roughly a third.

The UKPDS 34 trial in The Lancet showed that metformin reduced diabetes-related mortality by 42 percent in overweight patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes compared with conventional diet-only therapy.
Metformin cuts diabetes-related mortality by about 42 percent in overweight adults with new type 2 diabetes compared with diet alone.
The EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial reported in NEJM in 2015 that empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death by 38 percent in patients with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
Empagliflozin lowers cardiovascular death by around 38 percent in people with type 2 diabetes who already have cardiovascular disease.
The STEP 1 trial of semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly, published in NEJM in 2021, achieved a mean body weight reduction of 14.9 percent over 68 weeks in adults with obesity but without diabetes.
Weekly 2.4 mg semaglutide produces an average 15 percent body weight loss over 68 weeks in adults with obesity and no diabetes.
A BMJ meta-analysis of randomized trials found that levothyroxine replacement for subclinical hypothyroidism in adults over 65 did not improve quality-of-life or thyroid-related symptoms.
Treating subclinical hypothyroidism in older adults with levothyroxine does not meaningfully improve symptoms or quality of life.
The PREDIMED trial in NEJM reported that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil or mixed nuts reduced major cardiovascular events by about 30 percent in high-risk adults.
A Mediterranean diet enriched with extra-virgin olive oil or mixed nuts cuts major cardiovascular events by roughly 30 percent in high-risk adults.
A Cochrane review of sodium reduction trials concluded that modest salt restriction lowers systolic blood pressure by about 4 to 5 mmHg in hypertensive adults.
Cutting dietary salt by a modest amount lowers systolic blood pressure by roughly 4 to 5 mmHg in people with hypertension.
The VITAL trial in NEJM found that vitamin D3 2000 IU daily did not reduce incident invasive cancer or major cardiovascular events over 5 years in generally healthy adults.
Taking 2000 IU of vitamin D3 every day does not lower cancer incidence or major cardiovascular events in generally healthy adults over about five years.

The STAR*D study reported in the American Journal of Psychiatry that only about one third of patients with major depression achieve remission on an initial SSRI, with cumulative remission reaching roughly 67 percent after four sequential treatment steps.
Only about a third of people with major depression reach remission on their first SSRI; with up to four sequential treatment steps, cumulative remission approaches two-thirds.
The NICE guideline NG222 on depression in adults recommends cognitive behavioural therapy or an SSRI as a first-line option for moderate depression, citing equivalent short-term efficacy.
For moderate adult depression, cognitive behavioural therapy and SSRIs work about equally well in the short term and either can be offered first line.

A Lancet Psychiatry systematic review of means restriction interventions reported that restricting access to highly lethal methods, especially firearms and pesticides, produces measurable reductions in overall suicide rates.
Restricting access to highly lethal suicide methods, particularly firearms and pesticides, reliably lowers overall suicide rates.

The AAP Task Force on Sudden Infant Death Syndrome recommends that infants be placed supine for every sleep period, a practice associated with more than a 50 percent drop in SIDS incidence since the Back to Sleep campaign began in 1994.
Putting babies on their backs for every sleep has halved SIDS rates since the early 1990s and remains the standard recommendation.
The WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life, with continued breastfeeding alongside appropriate complementary foods up to two years or beyond.
Infants should be exclusively breastfed for their first six months, with breastfeeding continuing alongside complementary foods up to age two or later.
The AAP clinical practice guideline on bronchiolitis recommends against routine use of bronchodilators, corticosteroids, or chest physiotherapy in infants with typical viral bronchiolitis.
In infants with typical viral bronchiolitis, bronchodilators, corticosteroids, and chest physiotherapy are not recommended as routine treatments.

WHO and UNICEF guidance establishes low-osmolarity oral rehydration solution as first-line therapy for acute diarrhoea in children, reducing the need for intravenous fluids and shortening diarrhoea duration.
Low-osmolarity oral rehydration solution is the first-line treatment for children with acute diarrhoea and cuts both IV fluid use and diarrhoea duration.
The APPAC trial in JAMA showed that antibiotic therapy alone successfully treated roughly 73 percent of adults with uncomplicated acute appendicitis at five-year follow-up, avoiding surgery.
About 73 percent of adults with uncomplicated acute appendicitis can be treated with antibiotics alone and avoid surgery through five years of follow-up.

A New England Journal of Medicine study by Haynes et al. reported that implementing the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist was associated with a drop in inpatient surgical mortality from 1.5 to 0.8 percent across eight participating hospitals.
Rolling out the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist has been shown to cut inpatient surgical mortality from about 1.5 percent to under 1 percent.
The ACCP CHEST guidelines recommend pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in most hospitalized medical and surgical patients at moderate to high thrombotic risk.
Most hospitalized medical and surgical patients at moderate to high clot risk should receive pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis.
The MRC Vitamin Study, published in The Lancet in 1991, showed that preconception folic acid supplementation reduced the recurrence of neural tube defects by 72 percent.
Taking folic acid before and during early pregnancy cuts the recurrence of neural tube defects by about 72 percent.
The Magpie trial in The Lancet established that magnesium sulfate more than halves the risk of eclampsia in women with pre-eclampsia and reduces maternal mortality.
Magnesium sulfate cuts the risk of eclampsia by more than half in women with pre-eclampsia and also lowers maternal mortality.
A Cochrane review confirms that a single course of antenatal corticosteroids given to women at risk of preterm birth reduces neonatal respiratory distress syndrome and neonatal death.
A single course of antenatal corticosteroids for women likely to deliver preterm reduces newborn respiratory distress syndrome and neonatal death.
The USPSTF recommends screening for gestational diabetes in asymptomatic pregnant women at or after 24 weeks of gestation, citing moderate net benefit.
Asymptomatic pregnant women should be screened for gestational diabetes starting at 24 weeks of gestation.
The RE-LY trial in NEJM showed that dabigatran 150 mg twice daily reduced stroke or systemic embolism in atrial fibrillation compared with warfarin, without increasing major bleeding.
In atrial fibrillation, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily prevents more strokes and systemic emboli than warfarin without raising major bleeding.

A BMJ cohort study reported that long-term proton-pump inhibitor use was associated with a modestly increased risk of hip fracture, Clostridioides difficile infection, and community-acquired pneumonia.
Long-term proton-pump inhibitor use is linked to modestly higher risks of hip fracture, C. difficile infection, and community-acquired pneumonia.
The IDSA guideline on antimicrobial stewardship documents that formal stewardship programmes reduce inappropriate antibiotic use and lower C. difficile infection rates in hospitals.
Hospital antimicrobial stewardship programmes cut inappropriate antibiotic use and drop C. difficile infection rates.
The ISIS-1 trial in The Lancet showed that early intravenous atenolol after acute myocardial infarction reduced 7-day vascular mortality by about 15 percent.
Giving intravenous atenolol early after an acute myocardial infarction cuts 7-day vascular mortality by around 15 percent.
Doll and Hill's 50-year cohort study of British doctors in the BMJ concluded that lifelong smokers lose on average 10 years of life expectancy compared with never-smokers.
Lifelong smokers lose about ten years of life expectancy on average compared with people who never smoked.
A Cochrane review of seatbelt laws and use concluded that wearing a seatbelt reduces the risk of death in a motor-vehicle crash by approximately 45 percent for front-seat occupants.
Wearing a seatbelt cuts the risk of death in a car crash by roughly 45 percent for front-seat occupants.
The Global Burden of Disease 2019 study in The Lancet ranked high systolic blood pressure as the single largest contributor to global disability-adjusted life years lost.
High systolic blood pressure is the single biggest driver of global disability-adjusted life years lost.
The WHO 2021 air quality guidelines state that long-term exposure to PM2.5 above 5 micrograms per cubic metre is associated with measurable increases in cardiovascular and respiratory mortality.
Long-term exposure to fine particulate PM2.5 above 5 micrograms per cubic metre raises cardiovascular and respiratory mortality.

The WHO 2020 Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour recommend that adults do 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity per week.
Adults should aim for 150 to 300 minutes of moderate aerobic activity or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous activity per week.
The USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all adults about tobacco use and provide behavioural interventions plus FDA-approved pharmacotherapy to those who smoke.
Clinicians should ask every adult about tobacco use and offer behavioural counselling plus FDA-approved pharmacotherapy to smokers.
The USPSTF 2022 recommendation supports low- to moderate-dose statin therapy for adults aged 40 to 75 with at least one cardiovascular risk factor and a 10-year ASCVD risk of 10 percent or higher.
Adults aged 40 to 75 with at least one cardiovascular risk factor and a 10-year ASCVD risk of 10 percent or more should be offered low- to moderate-dose statin therapy.
A Lancet analysis from the Global Burden of Disease study concluded that the safest level of alcohol consumption for overall health is zero drinks per week.
From a pure population-health standpoint, the safest amount of alcohol to drink per week is zero.

The PARADIGM-HF trial in NEJM demonstrated that sacubitril-valsartan reduced the combined endpoint of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization by 20 percent compared with enalapril in HFrEF.
In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, sacubitril-valsartan cuts the combined risk of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization by about 20 percent versus enalapril.
WHO position on BCG vaccination holds that a single neonatal dose provides substantial protection against disseminated tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis in children.
A single neonatal BCG dose offers strong protection against disseminated TB and TB meningitis in children.
The EBCTCG meta-analysis in The Lancet showed that five years of adjuvant tamoxifen reduced 15-year breast cancer mortality by about one third in women with ER-positive early breast cancer.
Five years of adjuvant tamoxifen cuts 15-year breast cancer mortality by roughly a third in women with ER-positive early breast cancer.
A Cochrane review of lithium in bipolar disorder concluded that long-term lithium therapy reduces the rate of manic and depressive relapses and lowers suicide risk compared with placebo.
Long-term lithium therapy in bipolar disorder reduces manic and depressive relapses and lowers suicide risk.
The WHO REPLACE action package documents that eliminating industrial trans fats from the food supply can prevent more than 500,000 deaths from coronary heart disease globally each year.
Removing industrial trans fats from the food supply could prevent over half a million coronary heart disease deaths worldwide every year.

The WHO MPOWER package reports that raising tobacco taxes so that excise represents at least 75 percent of the retail price is the single most cost-effective intervention to reduce tobacco consumption.
Pushing tobacco excise taxes to at least 75 percent of the retail price is the most cost-effective way to cut smoking rates at the population level.

According to Tacitus in the Annals Book 15 chapters 38 to 44, Emperor Nero blamed the Christians of Rome for the fire that broke out in July of 64 CE and subjected them to elaborate public executions in the imperial gardens.
After the Great Fire of Rome broke out in July 64 CE, Emperor Nero blamed the city's Christian population and had many of them executed in brutal public spectacles held in the imperial gardens.

Thucydides, in History of the Peloponnesian War Book 2 chapter 47, records that a devastating pestilence struck Athens in the second year of the war, beginning in Piraeus and sweeping through the overcrowded city during the summer of 430 BCE.
A devastating plague struck Athens in 430 BCE during the second year of the Peloponnesian War, first appearing in the port of Piraeus before sweeping through the overcrowded city.
Herodotus records in Histories Book 7 chapter 228 that King Leonidas and three hundred Spartans died holding the pass at Thermopylae against Xerxes' invading Persian army in 480 BCE.
In 480 BCE King Leonidas led three hundred Spartans to their deaths defending the narrow pass at Thermopylae against the invading Persian army of Xerxes.

Plutarch's Life of Caesar chapter 66 narrates that on the Ides of March in 44 BCE a conspiracy of senators led by Brutus and Cassius stabbed Julius Caesar to death at the foot of Pompey's statue in the Curia.
On the Ides of March in 44 BCE a conspiracy of Roman senators led by Brutus and Cassius assassinated Julius Caesar at the foot of Pompey's statue inside the Curia.

Suetonius in The Twelve Caesars, Life of Caligula chapter 55, reports that the emperor Caligula lavished such affection on his racehorse Incitatus that he gave the animal a marble stable, purple blankets, and reportedly intended to appoint it to the consulship.
The emperor Caligula was said to have given his racehorse Incitatus a marble stable with purple blankets and to have planned to appoint the animal to the Roman consulship.
Flavius Josephus records in The Jewish War Book 6 that Roman legions under Titus breached the walls of Jerusalem and destroyed the Second Temple during the siege of 70 CE.
In 70 CE Roman legions commanded by Titus breached the walls of Jerusalem and destroyed the Second Temple during the final siege of the city.

Livy's Ab Urbe Condita Book 21 recounts that in the autumn of 218 BCE Hannibal led a Carthaginian army together with war elephants over the Alps into northern Italy, opening the Second Punic War on Roman soil.
In the autumn of 218 BCE Hannibal led a Carthaginian army and his war elephants across the Alps into northern Italy to open the Second Punic War on Roman territory.

Bede's Ecclesiastical History of the English People Book 3 chapter 25 describes the Synod of Whitby in 664, where King Oswiu of Northumbria ruled in favour of Roman practice for calculating the date of Easter over the Ionan Celtic custom.
At the Synod of Whitby in 664 King Oswiu of Northumbria decided in favour of the Roman method for calculating the date of Easter over the Ionan Celtic custom.
The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle entry for the year 793 reports that heathen men miserably destroyed God's church on the island of Lindisfarne through rapine and slaughter on the eighth of June.
On 8 June 793 Viking raiders sacked the monastery on the island of Lindisfarne, an event widely taken to mark the opening of the Viking Age in the British Isles.

Einhard's Vita Karoli Magni chapter 28 describes how Pope Leo III placed a crown on the head of Charlemagne in Saint Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day of the year 800, acclaiming him emperor of the Romans.
On Christmas Day in the year 800 Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor of the Romans in Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome.

William of Malmesbury in Gesta Regum Anglorum Book 3 describes how William the Conqueror defeated King Harold Godwinson at the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066, with Harold slain as the English line broke at dusk.
At the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066 William the Conqueror defeated King Harold Godwinson, who was killed as the English shield wall collapsed at dusk.

Marco Polo's The Travels Book 2 describes the splendour of Kublai Khan's summer capital at Xanadu, where the Great Khan maintained a pleasure palace of marble and gold surrounded by a walled hunting park.
Kublai Khan maintained a summer capital at Xanadu containing a marble and gold pleasure palace set within a walled hunting park.

Ibn Battuta's Rihla recounts his visit to the Mali Empire in 1352 and 1353, where he described the court of Mansa Sulayman and praised the safety of travel and the strict administration of justice in the realm.
Between 1352 and 1353 the traveller Ibn Battuta visited the Mali Empire and remarked on the safety of its roads and the strict administration of justice under Mansa Sulayman.
Jean Froissart's Chronicles Book 1 describes how English longbowmen under King Edward III cut down the flower of French chivalry at the Battle of Crecy on 26 August 1346.
At the Battle of Crecy on 26 August 1346 English longbowmen serving King Edward III decimated the French mounted knights during the Hundred Years War.
The text of Magna Carta as sealed at Runnymede on 15 June 1215 constrains King John in clause 39 to judge no free man except by the lawful judgement of his peers or by the law of the land.
On 15 June 1215 at Runnymede King John sealed Magna Carta, whose clause 39 barred the king from judging any free man except by the lawful judgement of his peers or by the law of the land.

Bartolome de las Casas in A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies, published in 1552, catalogued the massacres, enslavement, and forced labour inflicted by Spanish conquerors on the indigenous peoples of Hispaniola and Cuba.
Spanish colonists during the early sixteenth century inflicted massacres, enslavement, and forced labour on the indigenous peoples of Hispaniola and Cuba during the conquest of the Caribbean.

Bernal Diaz del Castillo in The True History of the Conquest of New Spain chapter 87 recounts the awed first sight of Tenochtitlan in November 1519, with its causeways and lake city appearing to the Spaniards like an enchantment from the tale of Amadis.
In November 1519 the Spanish expedition under Hernan Cortes first glimpsed the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan rising from Lake Texcoco with its long stone causeways.

Samuel Pepys' diary entry for 2 September 1666 records that a fire beginning in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane spread rapidly through the timber houses of the City of London while the Lord Mayor dithered.
On 2 September 1666 the Great Fire of London broke out in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane and spread rapidly through the timber buildings of the City.

Galileo Galilei's Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems, published in Florence in 1632, presents Salviati, Sagredo, and Simplicio arguing over three days on the merits of the Ptolemaic and Copernican cosmologies.
Galileo Galilei published the Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems in Florence in 1632, staging a three-day debate between defenders of the Ptolemaic and Copernican cosmologies.
Thomas Hobbes in Leviathan chapter 13, first published in 1651, argues that life outside political society is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
Thomas Hobbes argued in 1651 that human life outside organised political society would be solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
John Locke in the Second Treatise of Government chapter 5, published in 1689, argues that property originates in the labour that a person mixes with previously common resources.
John Locke argued in 1689 that private property originates when a person mixes their own labour with previously common resources.
Edward Gibbon in The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire chapter 38, published between 1776 and 1789, attributes the long decline of Rome to the triumph of barbarism and religion.
Edward Gibbon famously attributed the long decline of Rome to what he called the triumph of barbarism and religion.

Thomas Paine's pamphlet Common Sense, published anonymously in Philadelphia in January 1776, argued that hereditary monarchy was an absurdity and that the American colonies should declare independence from Great Britain.
In January 1776 Thomas Paine anonymously published a pamphlet in Philadelphia arguing against hereditary monarchy and for American independence from Great Britain.

Alexis de Tocqueville in Democracy in America Volume 1, published in 1835, observes that the equality of social conditions is the generative fact from which all the peculiarities of American political life proceed.
Alexis de Tocqueville argued in 1835 that the equality of social conditions was the foundational feature from which the peculiarities of American political life flowed.
Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels in The Communist Manifesto, first printed in London in February 1848, opened with the declaration that a spectre was haunting Europe, namely the spectre of communism.
Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published The Communist Manifesto in London in February 1848, famously opening with the image of communism as a spectre haunting Europe.
Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, published by John Murray on 24 November 1859, set out a theory of descent with modification by means of natural selection operating on heritable variation.
Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, released on 24 November 1859, presented the theory of descent with modification through natural selection acting on heritable variation.

Frederick Douglass' Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave, published in Boston in 1845, recounts his birth into slavery on a Maryland plantation and his eventual escape north in 1838.
Frederick Douglass was born into slavery on a Maryland plantation and escaped north in 1838 before becoming a leading abolitionist orator and writer.

The text of Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address as delivered on 19 November 1863 at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery dedicates the nation to the unfinished work of ensuring that government of the people, by the people, and for the people shall not perish from the earth.

On 19 November 1863 Abraham Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery, closing with a pledge that government of the people, by the people, and for the people shall not perish from the earth.

Friedrich Engels in The Condition of the Working Class in England in 1844, published in German in Leipzig in 1845, catalogued the slums, disease, and child labour produced by the industrial economy of Manchester.
Friedrich Engels in 1845 catalogued the slums, disease, and child labour produced by the industrial economy of Manchester in the early years of the factory system.

Eric Hobsbawm in Age of Extremes: The Short Twentieth Century 1914-1991, published in 1994, argued that the period between the outbreak of the First World War and the dissolution of the Soviet Union formed a coherent historical epoch.
The historian Eric Hobsbawm argued that the years from the outbreak of the First World War in 1914 to the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991 constituted a coherent short twentieth century.

Winston Churchill in The Second World War Volume 1 chapter 19 describes the policy of appeasement pursued by Neville Chamberlain at the Munich Conference of September 1938, which ceded the Sudetenland to Nazi Germany without Czech consent.
At the Munich Conference of September 1938 Neville Chamberlain pursued a policy of appeasement that ceded the Czechoslovak Sudetenland to Nazi Germany without Czech consent.

William Shirer in The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich, published in 1960, recounts how the Reichstag fire on the night of 27 February 1933 was used by the Nazi leadership to justify emergency decrees suspending German civil liberties.
The Reichstag fire on the night of 27 February 1933 was used by the Nazi leadership as pretext for emergency decrees that suspended German civil liberties.

Primo Levi in If This Is a Man, first published in Italian as Se questo e un uomo in 1947, records his deportation to the Auschwitz Monowitz labour camp in February 1944 and his survival until liberation by Soviet forces in January 1945.
The chemist Primo Levi was deported to the Auschwitz Monowitz labour camp in February 1944 and survived until the camp's liberation by Soviet forces in January 1945.

George Kennan's Long Telegram, sent from the United States embassy in Moscow on 22 February 1946, argued that Soviet conduct was driven by a traditional Russian insecurity overlaid with Marxist ideology and recommended a policy of long-term patient containment.

On 22 February 1946 the American diplomat George Kennan argued from Moscow that Soviet conduct was driven by traditional Russian insecurity and Marxist ideology, and he proposed a policy of long-term containment.

A. J. P. Taylor in The Origins of the Second World War, published in 1961, provocatively argued that Hitler was in many respects an ordinary opportunist German statesman rather than a uniquely demonic planner of general war.

The historian A. J. P. Taylor provocatively argued in 1961 that Adolf Hitler behaved in many respects as an opportunistic German statesman rather than as a uniquely premeditated planner of general war.

Gabriel Kolko in Anatomy of a War: Vietnam, the United States, and the Modern Historical Experience, published in 1985, argued that American intervention in Vietnam grew out of a broader Cold War strategy of managing Third World nationalism.
The historian Gabriel Kolko argued that American intervention in Vietnam grew out of a broader Cold War strategy aimed at managing Third World nationalism.

Ibn Khaldun in the Muqaddimah, completed in 1377, develops the concept of asabiyyah or group solidarity as the engine by which rural tribal coalitions conquer sedentary dynasties and in turn decline after three generations.

The fourteenth-century historian Ibn Khaldun developed the concept of asabiyyah, a form of group solidarity by which rural tribal coalitions conquered settled dynasties before themselves declining after about three generations.

Sima Qian in the Shiji or Records of the Grand Historian, completed around 94 BCE, narrates the unification of China under the First Emperor of Qin in 221 BCE and the standardisation of script, currency, and axle widths.
The First Emperor of Qin unified China in 221 BCE and ordered the standardisation of script, currency, and cart axle widths across his new empire.
The Nihon Shoki, completed in 720 CE, records the traditional date of 660 BCE for the accession of the legendary emperor Jimmu as the first sovereign of Yamato Japan.
Japanese imperial tradition, as preserved in eighth-century chronicles, assigned the year 660 BCE to the accession of the legendary emperor Jimmu as first sovereign of Yamato.

Wang Gungwu in The Chinese Overseas: From Earthbound China to the Quest for Autonomy, published in 2000, traces the long history of Chinese migration to Southeast Asia from the maritime networks of the Ming dynasty through the coolie trade of the nineteenth century.
Chinese migration to Southeast Asia stretches from the maritime trading networks of the Ming dynasty through the nineteenth-century coolie trade to the modern diaspora communities of the region.

Jacob Burckhardt in The Civilization of the Renaissance in Italy, published in Basel in 1860, argued that fifteenth-century Italy was the birthplace of the modern conception of the individual as distinct from the corporate and religious identities of medieval Europe.
The Swiss historian Jacob Burckhardt argued in 1860 that fifteenth-century Italy gave birth to the modern conception of the individual distinct from medieval corporate and religious identities.

Johan Huizinga in The Autumn of the Middle Ages, first published in Dutch in 1919 as Herfsttij der Middeleeuwen, portrayed fourteenth and fifteenth-century Burgundy and France as an overripe culture preoccupied with death, chivalric ritual, and spectacle.
The historian Johan Huizinga portrayed fourteenth and fifteenth-century Burgundy and France as an overripe culture preoccupied with death, chivalric ritual, and elaborate public spectacle.

E. P. Thompson in The Making of the English Working Class, published in 1963, argued that the English working class was not passively produced by industrialisation but actively made itself through political struggle between 1780 and 1832.

The historian E. P. Thompson argued that the English working class actively made itself through political struggle between roughly 1780 and 1832 rather than being passively produced by industrialisation.

Edward Said in Orientalism, published in 1978, argued that European scholarship about the Middle East from the late eighteenth century onward constructed the Orient as the West's civilisational opposite in order to legitimise imperial rule.

Edward Said argued in 1978 that European scholarship about the Middle East from the late eighteenth century onward constructed the Orient as a civilisational opposite of the West in ways that legitimised imperial rule.

Fernand Braudel in The Mediterranean and the Mediterranean World in the Age of Philip II, published in French in 1949, divided historical time into three layers: the longue duree of geography, the medium-term rhythms of social and economic structure, and the short-term events of political history.

Fernand Braudel's 1949 study of the sixteenth-century Mediterranean introduced a three-layered conception of historical time that distinguished geographical longue duree, medium-term socioeconomic rhythms, and short-term political events.

Leonard Woolley's Ur Excavations Volume 2: The Royal Cemetery, published in 1934, documents sixteen richly furnished royal tombs at Ur dating to around 2600 BCE, including that of Queen Puabi with her gold headdress and accompanying retainers.
Excavations at Ur uncovered sixteen richly furnished royal tombs dating to around 2600 BCE, among them the burial of Queen Puabi with her gold headdress and the remains of accompanying retainers.

Howard Carter in The Tomb of Tutankhamen Volume 1, published in 1923, describes opening the sealed door of KV62 in the Valley of the Kings on 26 November 1922 and glimpsing wonderful things by the light of a candle.
On 26 November 1922 the archaeologist Howard Carter opened the sealed door of tomb KV62 in the Valley of the Kings and famously reported seeing wonderful things in the antechamber of Tutankhamun.

Heinrich Schliemann in Troy and Its Remains, published in 1875, reports his discovery of a hoard of gold jewellery at the site of Hisarlik in 1873 which he identified, incorrectly, with the treasure of King Priam of Homeric Troy.
In 1873 Heinrich Schliemann uncovered a hoard of gold jewellery at the site of Hisarlik and mistakenly identified it with the treasure of King Priam of Homeric Troy.

Jean-Francois Champollion announced in his Lettre a M. Dacier of September 1822 that the hieroglyphic, demotic, and Greek registers of the Rosetta Stone could be decoded through phonetic readings of royal cartouches such as those of Ptolemy and Cleopatra.

In September 1822 the French scholar Jean-Francois Champollion announced that Egyptian hieroglyphs could be deciphered through phonetic readings of royal cartouches such as those of Ptolemy and Cleopatra on the Rosetta Stone.

Mary Leakey in a 1979 article in National Geographic Magazine reported the discovery of a 27 metre trail of hominin footprints preserved in volcanic ash at Laetoli in Tanzania, dated to approximately 3.6 million years ago.
